assessments.reasoning: At the pinned commit, json/details/OSL-1.1.json gives OSL-1.1, “Open Software License 1.1” and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Both crossRef and seeAlso cite https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Licensing/OSL1.1.
The official unsigned annotated tag names v3.29.0 and gives object.type=commit and object.sha=31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. This is the revision serving the 1.1 detail.
OSI’s archived article specifies 1.1 in its heading and operative notice, despite its unversioned PHP path. That supplies the publisher side of the mapping.

Fedora’s own XML export identifies page 7956, revision 66761, and records the move from Licensing/OSL1.1 to Licensing:OSL1.1. Its 52-byte application notice has the same range digest as the OSI notice.

challenge.method: Checked the release target, detail fields, Fedora namespace move and the notice in all three documents. Compared section 11 as a test of full-text equality.
challenge.results: All three identify version 1.1. Fedora and SPDX show “å¤” in the statutory citation where OSI HTML has §. The edition mapping survives this transcription difference. SPDX’s false approval field cannot settle Rosen’s retrospective board account.

limitations: Fedora reproduces the license and shares its documentary lineage. Its reproduction supplies neither independent legal authority nor an OSI approval decision.
reasoning: SPDX assigns OSL-1.1 to Open Software License 1.1 and cites Fedora’s reproduction. Fedora’s page-move record connects the cited path to the inspected export, whose heading and notice agree with the archived OSI article.
